details: The functions comparing vectors. Cosine (angle only) is the default for normalized text embeddings; dot product incorporates magnitude; Euclidean measures raw distance. Must match how the embedding model was trained.

explainer.lead: These are the concrete functions that compare embedding vectors, and the choice changes what 'similar' means. Picking the wrong one quietly degrades search and matching quality.

tiers.eli5: Different rulers for comparing arrows: one only checks the direction they point, one also counts how long they are.
tiers.practitioner: Cosine is the default for normalised text embeddings, dot product folds in magnitude, and Euclidean measures raw distance. The pitfall is using a metric the embedding model was not trained with.
tiers.paperLevel: Cosine compares angle only, dot product multiplies magnitudes as well, and Euclidean gives straight-line distance; the metric must match the model's training objective.

explainer.example: Two normalised sentence embeddings are scored with cosine, so only their direction matters and length differences are ignored.
